subject: Banking
title: The South Sea Bubble
description: A fast breakdown of The South Sea Bubble for builders.

hook.text: In 1720, the South Sea Company promised investors riches from trade. Its stock rose 800% before crashing to nothing.

buildup.text: The British government let the company take over national debt.

discovery.text: The company had almost no real trade revenue. The stock price was pure speculation fed by insider manipulation.

twist.text: Isaac Newton invested early, sold for a profit, then reinvested near the peak and lost £20,000 — a fortune at the time.

climax.text: Even a genius couldn't resist the bubble. The South Sea crash proved that herd behavior defeats individual intelligence.

punchline.text: Newton lost a fortune. The South Sea Bubble defeated even genius.

quiz.question: What happened to Isaac Newton during the South Sea Bubble?
options: He sold at a profit then reinvested near the peak and lost £20,000
